title: NOAA: El Niño and La Niña are the warm and cool phases of ENSO
summary: NOAA describes ENSO as a tropical Pacific pattern that shifts irregularly every two to seven years.
body: NOAA Climate.gov says El Niño and La Niña are the warm and cool phases of a natural climate pattern across the tropical Pacific called the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, or ENSO. It says the pattern shifts back and forth irregularly every two to seven years, changes ocean temperature, and disrupts the usual wind and rainfall patterns across the tropics, with further effects outside the tropics. The fetched page is an archived Climate.gov copy. This card uses the definition on that page, not a later monthly advisory.
